ev.q: Influenza vaccination coverage was higher among non-Hispanic White (White) and non-Hispanic Asian (Asian) adults than among most other racial and ethnic groups.
a higher percentage of White adults reported that they probably or definitely will not receive a COVID-19 vaccine (43.2%) than did Black (31.3%)

changes.why: Group values are set side by side and judged by t-tests, but no difference or ratio is reported, so scale is null; this also matches the level-2 cap in equity.

equity.level_reason: Coverage and intent are reported by race/ethnicity, insurance and urbanicity, and the discussion speaks of racial and ethnic disparities, but contrasts are only side-by-side values or significance-based wording with no computed difference, ratio or shortfall.

level_alternative.reason: The disparity is explicitly framed and interpreted (potential coverage for Hispanic, Black and Asian adults similar to White), and a reader could treat tested group differences as quantified.

equity.equity_measurement: Race contrasts use White adults as the implicit referent, with group differences judged by t-tests but not reported as differences; insurance and urbanicity appear only in Figure 2 and one sentence each. Incarcerated and institutionalized adults are outside the sample frame.

notes: Programmatic measures (free vaccines, trusted messengers, Bridge Access Program) appear only as recommendations, so determinants_of_health stays null.
